chapter: Early life and the plantation brass band
title: Labor Day parades in New Orleans and the Elks and Grove halls
summary: The plantation band came up to New Orleans for Labor Day parades. The bands gathered at the Elks hall and at Grove Hall on St. Peter Street. The brass band also played dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: We always had the privilege. We could get off and go and play. That's what we had. Did your band ever come up here for Mardi Gras or Carnival? Did you ever have any parades up in New Orleans? On Labor Day. Labor Day. Labor Day.
Labor Day we had parades up there. Your band would come up here?
For Labor Day. Yeah. We'd right there at the business at the Elk Street. At a hall that's called Elk. We used to meet there. All the bands used to meet up there together.
There was an old hall there at Globe Hall too, was there?
The Grove Hall was out there on St. Peter Street. St. Peter. Yeah. Out there near the basement. What they used to call it the basement. Yes. It was right off from that auditorium.
Right where the auditorium is. Yeah.

Now you must be known up top of them. Yes, I never knew that hall. People tell us about that hall. Yeah. Used to call it the Grove Hall. Did you ever play any dance work any place for dances or just the brass band? Oh, brass band used to play the dances. They played the dances too? Sure.
